holidays.name: Presidential Joke Day
holidays.description: A day for sharing lighthearted political humor and laughing at the folks in the highest office, no matter which party you favor. Bring your best one-liners to the water cooler.
holidays.origin: A largely unofficial observance listed in quirky-holiday calendars, tied to the long American tradition of poking fun at presidents and politicians.
holidays.funFact: Presidential humor goes way back: Abraham Lincoln was famous for telling funny stories, often to defuse tension in tense Cabinet meetings.

holidays.name: Son and Daughter Day
holidays.description: A day for parents to celebrate their kids with no strings attached, with no chores, no lectures, and plenty of quality time together.
holidays.origin: An unofficial family observance that grew through greeting card and parenting calendars as a way to flip the script on Mother's and Father's Day.
holidays.funFact: Some versions of this observance are celebrated on August 11 while other calendars list it in different months, since it has no single official sponsor.

holidays.name: Raspberry Bombe Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the fancy, dome-shaped frozen dessert layered with raspberry ice cream, sorbet, and sometimes cake or chocolate. Perfect for impressing dinner guests with minimal effort.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday from dessert calendars honoring the bombe, a classic French dessert molded in a spherical dish.
holidays.funFact: The word bombe comes from the French word for bomb, because the dessert was originally molded in a round, cannonball-shaped mold.

holidays.name: Play in the Sand Day
holidays.description: A day to ditch your inhibitions and dig, build, and sculpt in the sand like a kid again, whether at a beach, a sandbox, or a backyard pile.
holidays.origin: An unofficial summer observance popular on fun-day calendars, encouraging adults and children alike to get a little messy outdoors.
holidays.funFact: Professional sand sculptors use a special blend of fine sand and water, and some of their castles can rise over 40 feet tall.

holidays.name: Hip Hop Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the birth of hip hop culture, including rapping, DJing, breakdancing, and graffiti art, which grew from a Bronx party into a worldwide phenomenon.
holidays.origin: On August 11, 1973, DJ Kool Herc threw a back-to-school party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx, where he extended instrumental breaks using two turntables, which is widely considered the birth of hip hop.
holidays.funFact: The party was organized by Kool Herc's sister Cindy Campbell to raise money for new school clothes, and the building is now recognized as a historic landmark.
